en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Sixth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether the Eye Faculty is Visible, etc.:
Is the eye faculty visible? Yes.
"Is form the sense-sphere of form, the element of form …pe… does it come within the range of the eye?
One should not say so …pe….
Is the eye-faculty visible?
Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on both the eye and the eye-faculty? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does visual consciousness arise dependent on both the eye and the eye-faculty?
Yes.
“Dependent upon the eye and the eye-faculty, eye-consciousness arises”—
is there such a sutta? No,
there is not.
“Dependent upon the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises”—
is there such a sutta? Yes.
If the sutta passage, “Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises,” is indeed authentic,
then surely it should not be said that “dependent on the eye and the eye-faculty, eye-consciousness arises.”
Is it not to be said that “the five faculties are visible”?
Yes, they are.
"Does the eye see, the ear, the nose, the tongue, and the body?
"Yes.
"If the eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, and the body see, then indeed, sir, you must say:"
“The five faculties are visible,” and so forth… The discussion beginning with “The eye-faculty is visible” is concluded.
